preamble: Depalatalization of the voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] to the alveolar affricate [dz]: the tongue body is lowered from the palatal region and the affricate is retracted to a plain alveolar articulation, keeping voicing and affrication. The defining case is Kashubian 'kaszëbienié' (Kashubization): the Proto-Slavic soft dentals t, d, s, z before front vowels first became alveolo-palatal [tɕ dʑ ɕ ʑ], as they still are in Polish, and then in Kashubian lost their palatality to [ts dz s z]. Kashubian therefore has dz where Polish has dź, as in dzéń 'day' against Polish dzień, and the depalatalization also caused following short i to shift to ë (chòdzëc against Polish chodzić). The change is confined to Kashubian, so it is rare.

examples.note: The alveolo-palatal affricate became plain alveolar [dz]; Polish preserves the earlier [dʑ].
After depalatalization the following short i became ë.
